title: Map symbol words in myth and folklore without predefined meanings
summary: Embed the passage around each of 20 symbol words, lay the passages out with UMAP and let HDBSCAN find groups, so any shared meaning has to come from the text.

title: The baseline clusters followed books, not symbols
summary: In the first run a cluster's largest book held 74 % of it on average, and only 5 of 43 clusters drew on several books.

title: Book identity confounds the representation
summary: Style, era and translation make passages from one book alike whatever symbol they hold, and that shared part drives the clusters.

title: Centre the embeddings by book before clustering
summary: Subtract each book's mean embedding and normalise again, and compare it with masking the symbol word on one shared sample.
reason: The baseline grouped books, so the part every passage of a book shares had to be removed before reading anything into the clusters.

title: Four deconfounding variants on one shared sample
summary: Baseline, symbol masked, book-centred and both, each with its own map and clusters on the same occurrences.
hypothesis: Removing each book's mean embedding should reduce how much a cluster depends on one book.

title: Book-centring cut the largest-book share from 74 % to 57 %
summary: Cross-book clusters rose from 5 to 24 and the silhouette did not drop. Masking the symbol word changed the book share little.

title: Glossaries and indexes formed false cross-book clusters
summary: One of the largest book-centred cross-book clusters was built from Bulfinch's glossary entries, not from narrative.

title: Remove paratext before clustering
summary: Cut contents, glossaries, notes and indexes from the books and keep an audit of every removal.

title: Only a person's review may name a cluster
summary: Clusters are ranked for review and stay numbers until someone has read the passages; rejections are recorded too.
reason: A cluster spanning several books is a recurring context worth reading, not proof of a shared meaning.

title: Expand the corpus to 101 books across 12 traditions
summary: Keep the same 20 symbols and grow the corpus from 10 to 101 public-domain books, so the comparison stays controlled.

title: The larger corpus gave broader but weaker structure
summary: Book-centred, the largest-book share fell to 36 % and 87 of 114 clusters span several books, while the silhouette fell to 0.31.

title: Four embedding models compared by their nearest neighbours
summary: MiniLM, bge-base, e5-base and gte-base on the same 21,898 book-centred passages, scored by the share of each passage's 10 nearest neighbours from the same book or with the same symbol.
hypothesis: A larger embedding model places passages more by symbol and less by book.

title: Larger models gained about four points on same-symbol neighbours
summary: gte-base put 31 % same-symbol passages among the neighbours against 26 % for MiniLM; same-book neighbours fell from 26 % to 22-25 %.

title: Keep all-MiniLM-L6-v2 for the published atlas
reason: The gain is small next to the book effect, and the clustering settings were chosen for MiniLM; they should change only after the review.

title: Which v4 clusters survive a person's review?
How often is a symbol word used literally rather than symbolically?
summary: Needs a hand-labelled sample of occurrences; none exists yet.

title: Open the concept layer with Concept Journey
summary: Follow one concept at a time through stories, philosophy, Riksdag speeches and the AI Act; the constellation stays as the exploring view.
reason: A reader can follow one idea across four kinds of text more easily than read the whole constellation at once.

title: Record why the system changes in an append-only Idea Lineage journal
summary: Ideas, decisions, experiments, findings and questions are stored as short structured events; prompts and conversations never are.
reason: Data lineage says where data came from; the reasons behind a change of direction were not written down anywhere.
